text:
Matthew Schaefer won the Calder Trophy last season, and the Islanders' answer has been to give him more. He's playing 26.8 minutes a night, 27.64 over his last 10, at 19. He has 16 points in 16 games, and NHL EDGE puts his top speed in the 98th percentile.

The underlying play is better than the scoreboard. With him on the ice at five-on-five, New York takes 56% of the shot attempts and 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), yet the Islanders have scored 4.48 fewer goals than those chances deserve. That's mostly the finishing around him, and it tends to even out. His own shooting is honest: 5 goals on 4.1 expected.

Off the ice, this was the week the Islanders, Northwell Health and Schaefer opened the Jennifer Schaefer Child Support Room, named for his late mother. On it, we'd watch the defensive side of a 27-minute job: Saturday's overtime loss to New Jersey ended on a Jack Hughes breakaway after Schaefer went down. "I thought I [got tripped], but I mean, they could have seen otherwise," he said, per NHL.com's Stefen Rosner.
headline: Schaefer at 19: 27 minutes and climbing
